blocks.text: After Configuring Tree Discovery in Zscaler and Deploying to AWS, do the following steps to complete the configuration:

blocks.item: 1. Select Accounts
In the Add to Monitoring Scope section, select the OUs or individual AWS accounts to monitor and click Next.
Click Select All to select all accounts, specific OUs, or individual accounts as required.
Enable the Autodetection toggle on for any OU to automatically discover and include new accounts added to that OU in the future.
2. Map Business Units
In the Business Unit Mapping section, select the AWS accounts and assign them to a business unit and click Next.
Use the column header checkbox to select all accounts at once.
Select Default if no custom business units are configured.
3. Select Services
In the Service Selection section, select the scanning services to enable and click Next. Metadata Scanning is enabled by default and is required. Select the following additional services as required:
Data Scanning: To enable scanning of data in cloud storage resources
Repository Scanning: To enable scanning of code repositories
Workload Scanning: To enable scanning of virtual machines and workloads
Enable Scanning of Encrypted Resources is enabled by default. Disable this option if you do not want Zscaler to scan encrypted resources.
4. Configure Settings
In the Configuration section, enter the following details and click Next.
For Automated Role Creation:
IAM Role Names: These role names are created across all monitored AWS accounts:
Asset Discovery Role Name: The name of the IAM role Zscaler creates for asset discovery.
Asset Scanning Role Name: The name of the IAM role Zscaler creates for asset scanning.
Role Tags (Optional): Add AWS tag key-value pairs to the IAM roles and policies, if required.
Manage CloudTrail Integration (Optional)
Trail S3 Bucket ARN: The ARN of the S3 bucket associated with your organization-level CloudTrail
Log Archive Account ID: The AWS Account ID where the CloudTrail S3 bucket resides
Evidence Storage (Optional)
Evidence S3 Bucket ARN: The ARN of the S3 bucket where evidence is stored.
Evidence Role Name: The name of the IAM role Zscaler creates to access the evidence S3 bucket.
Bucket Account ID: The AWS Account ID where the evidence S3 bucket resides.
See image.
For Manual Role Creation:

Provide pre-created IAM Role names: Enter the role names you've already created in each member account. Using the account IDs selected in Account Selection, the ARN is automatically constructed in the format arn:aws:iam::<memberAccountId>:role/<name>. Each role's trust policy must permit sts:AssumeRole from Zscaler, scoped to the provided External ID.
Asset Discovery Role Name: Enter the Asset Discovery Role Name.
Create the IAM role in the AWS console with the same name you entered for Asset Discovery Role Name.

Copy policy details available in the View Example Asset Discovery Role Configuration section in AI Security Console and paste them in the corresponding fields in the AWS Console while creating the IAM Role. To learn more, see Creating IAM Roles.
See image.
Scanning Role Name: Enter the scanning role name.
Create the IAM role in the AWS console with the same name you entered for Asset Discovery Role Name.

Copy policy details available in the View Example Scanning Role Configuration section in AI Security Console and paste them in the corresponding fields in the AWS Console while creating the IAM Role. To learn more, see Creating IAM Roles.
Role Tags (Optional): Custom AWS tags applied to every generated IAM role. To add custom tags, do the following:
Click Add Tag to enter a key and value pair for the tag.
Ensure to follow the guidelines while entering key-value pairs for custom tags.
Click Add Tag, and enter key-value pairs to add more tags.
Manage CloudTrail Integration (Optional but Recommended): Select the checkbox to enable this section. Enter the following information:
Organization Trail S3 Bucket ARN: Enter the S3 Bucket ARN used for Cloudtrail.
See image.
Log Archive Account ID: Enter the Log Archive Account ID.
Create the IAM role in the AWS console with the same name you entered for Asset Discovery Role Name.

Copy policy details available in the View Example CloudTrail Role Configuration section in AI Security Console and paste them in the corresponding fields in the AWS Console while creating the IAM Role. To learn more, see Creating IAM Roles.
See image.
Click Next.
See image.

blocks.text: After completing these steps, you are redirected to Deploying CloudFormation Templates in AWS & Validating in Zscaler.
